title: Rs 36 crore of diesel saved by tracking how RTC drivers drive

slides.head: Rs 36 crore of diesel saved by tracking how RTC drivers drive
What happened
slides.body: The system tracks gear choice, staying in the Green Band RPM range, idling, overspeeding and harsh braking; drivers get a grade and feedback after each duty.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: Fuel is one of the biggest running costs for a bus fleet, and TGSRTC says it is the first state RTC in India to use the system.

slides.head: Diesel saved every month
slides.body: Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka's RTCs have already asked TGSRTC how the system performs.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: i-ALERT buses save nearly 1,98,090 litres of diesel a month, TGSRTC says.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: TGSRTC's MD asked other wings to adopt similar tech; AP and Karnataka RTCs are studying the results. Ask: Do graded drivers get any reward, or only feedback?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
Rs 36 crore of diesel saved by tracking how RTC drivers drive

TGSRTC says i-ALERT, fitted in 1,500 Ashok Leyland BS-VI buses, grades every driver after duty and has saved about Rs 36 crore of diesel.

Why it matters: Fuel is one of the biggest running costs for a bus fleet, and TGSRTC says it is the first state RTC in India to use the system.

Source: Telangana Today. Image: Telangana Today
